source_snapshot.criteria: SOL (ttyS0) is set successfully at default 115200, correct output appears through SOL, and users can copy/paste between console and local system.
source_snapshot.script: No script; 20 attended and 20 machine minutes; the display code is reused by a future distinct variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES but wholly unrelated: it reads TEMP_UBB_FPGA over insecure SSH, truncates SDR output and provides no UART wiring, SOL session, 115200 or text-fidelity evidence.

old_problem: Items and Procedure define a physical BMC-console UART path, while Criteria names IPMI Serial-over-LAN and ttyS0 at 115200. These are not interchangeable standard identifiers: SOL is an IPMI/RMCP+ payload session, while ttyS0 denotes a Linux serial port. A platform may route them to the same console, but accepting that equivalence without a routing diagram could attach an electrically unsafe dongle, observe the wrong console or claim untested SOL coverage. DeepSeek's sensor query is unrelated to both branches.
disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending and Source Conflict. Authoritative standard documentation distinguishes SOL transport/session semantics from a Linux ttyS serial device but cannot decide the target platform's connector ownership or bridge routing. The owner must state whether this row validates physical BMC UART, SOL backed by ttyS0, a documented same endpoint, or two checkpoints. The Manual Only test contract can be fully parameterized around an owner-approved endpoint, wiring and harmless text oracle, so it is not irreducibly BLOCKED. Physical connection and live target/fidelity judgment remain human activities under ED-11/ED-17/ED-25; no SSH or sensor command can replace them.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1672, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, pending/conflict analyses, duplicate-code variants and ED-01 through ED-30 rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened as Functionality row 1673 / Wistron-BMC-00944-V004 / 773dd7f4c99d6e54.

The upstream ipmitool SOL implementation documentation defines SOL as an IPMI v2 payload over RMCP+ and starts it with `sol activate`; this is a network management session, not proof of a particular physical header. OpenBMC likewise documents an explicit protected `ipmitool ... sol activate` path.

Linux kernel serial-console documentation defines ttySx as a serial-port device and separates device identity from baud/parity/bits/flow-control options. The criteria's `ttyS0` and 115200 therefore name a logical device/configuration, but do not identify the board connector, voltage, pinout, console owner or SOL routing.

A physical BMC UART and an SOL console can expose the same byte stream only when platform firmware/routing documents prove that relationship. Readable text alone is insufficient because the wrong header or console can also produce plausible output.

The original bidirectional copy/paste coverage is retained as an exact harmless-marker byte/line-ending round trip, but only at a confirmed non-executing prompt. Credentials, shell commands, bootloader input and side-effecting text are prohibited.
The generic clear-logs step is excluded under ED-19. Pre-existing UART/BMC/host evidence remains intact; clearing does not improve console fidelity and would destroy diagnostic context.
The duplicate display code at Functionality row 1855 is a distinct Source Key/Variant and contributes no coverage or evidence to this row.

test_case.test_name: BMC UART — owner-resolved physical UART versus SOL/ttyS0 console fidelity
test_case.purpose: After the owner resolves the authoritative endpoint, have an authorized operator safely validate the intended BMC console at 115200 and demonstrate lossless bidirectional copy/paste of a harmless marker, while preserving the separate physical-UART and SOL identities unless a signed routing diagram proves equivalence.
required_package: Written scope ruling selecting physical BMC UART, IPMI SOL/ttyS0, a documented same endpoint, or separately accepted checkpoints; retain this Source Key/Variant independently from the duplicate code
Exact SUT/BMC/firmware identity and signed console-routing/ownership diagram; for physical UART, vendor header/connector, signal-voltage, pinout, ground, power-state and isolation specification

Approved isolated UART dongle/cable and terminal client, ESD controls, authorized operator and safe physical access; or owner-approved protected SOL transport, channel, privilege and credential method for a distinct SOL checkpoint
Signed 115200/parity/data/stop/flow-control/encoding/line-ending configuration, safe non-executing prompt and unique harmless marker/round-trip oracle
Visual/session capture, immutable evidence destination, clean close/disconnect steps and owner-approved electrical/session recovery
test_case.test_command: MANUAL ONLY after scope approval. For a physical-UART checkpoint, the operator independently verifies target/header/voltage/pinout/ground/power state, applies ESD controls, attaches only the approved isolated dongle, configures the signed 115200 serial parameters, visually identifies the intended live BMC console, and round-trips a unique harmless marker in both directions at a non-executing surface. For a separately approved SOL checkpoint, use the protected owner-specified equivalent of `ipmitool ... sol info` and `ipmitool ... sol activate`, identify the routed console and perform the same harmless marker check, then exit cleanly. Do not infer equivalence, run the DeepSeek sensor command, clear logs or paste credentials/executable input.
test_case.expected_result: Each owner-approved checkpoint connects to the exact intended console with the signed electrical or SOL path, reports/uses the approved 115200 serial configuration, produces stable readable target-specific output, and preserves the marker's exact characters, ordering and approved line endings in both directions without duplication, loss, garbling, unintended command execution or state change. The session closes and any physical dongle is safely disconnected. Physical UART evidence is not reported as SOL/ttyS0 proof unless signed routing evidence establishes the same endpoint.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Review remains PENDING until the owner resolves endpoint scope/routing. After binding, PASS requires operator-attended identity, safe connection/session evidence, exact configuration, live output and marker-fidelity observations for every selected checkpoint plus clean close/disconnect. A successful SSH/sensor command, readable text from an unidentified header, ipmitool exit zero, a static screenshot or unproved UART=SOL assumption is insufficient. Wrong/ambiguous target, unsafe wiring, garbling/loss/duplication, uncontrolled prompt or incomplete cleanup is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Never guess header, connector, voltage, pinout, ground, power-state or console ownership; stop before connection when the signed platform document is missing.
Physical attachment, target recognition, live interaction and disconnect are performed by an authorized operator with ESD/isolation controls; automation may only prepare/capture evidence.
Use only a harmless non-secret marker at a confirmed non-executing surface; never paste credentials, shell/bootloader commands, power/reset/storage/configuration text or secrets.
Do not treat SOL, ttyS0 and a board UART as equivalent without the signed routing diagram; keep separate evidence identities and outcomes.
Do not clear logs or automatically reconnect/retry after wrong target, electrical concern, garbling, session loss or unexpected prompt; preserve first evidence and stop.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/Variant, written endpoint ruling, target identity and signed console ownership/routing diagram
For physical UART: header/connector/voltage/pinout/ground/power-state proof, approved dongle identity and completed ESD/isolation checklist
For SOL if selected: protected transport/channel/privilege identity, complete `sol info` and session start/end evidence without exposed credentials
Terminal 115200/parity/data/stop/flow-control/encoding settings, redacted live target identity and byte/line-ending marker round-trip capture
No-log-clear/no-unintended-input audit, clean session close/dongle disconnect and engineer-owned PENDING/PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong or ambiguous console, unsafe voltage/pinout, garbled output, unexpected privileged surface, lost control or unintended input, stop typing immediately and preserve the capture. The operator follows the signed vendor power-safe disconnect or SOL-close procedure, verifies BMC/host state independently and escalates; do not reset, power-cycle, auto-reconnect or try alternate wiring. Any state change is recovered only by the platform owner using a separately approved procedure.

source_conflict.reason: The source's physical-dongle Procedure and SOL/ttyS0 Criteria define potentially different endpoints and evidence paths. Standard documentation clarifies the distinction but only project routing authority can decide whether they coincide or require separate checkpoints.

blocked.reason: The manual method, safety boundary, evidence and stop/recovery behavior are defined. Endpoint/routing/wiring values are normal owner-supplied Project inputs; execution becomes BLOCKED only if they cannot be established safely.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Written physical-UART-versus-SOL/ttyS0 scope ruling; exact target and console routing/ownership; vendor connector/voltage/pinout/ground/power-state data; approved dongle/ESD or SOL transport; signed 115200 framing/flow/encoding/line endings; safe prompt/marker; disconnect and recovery procedure.
pending.execution_status: REVIEW COMPLETE BUT ENGINEERING DECISION PENDING; EXECUTION NOT STARTED; NO UART CONNECTION, SOL SESSION, LOG CLEAR, BMC/DUT OR OTHER HARDWARE ACTION AUTHORIZED OR EXECUTED

external_authorities.application: Defines SOL as an IPMI v2 RMCP+ payload/session activated through the BMC, establishing that it is a specific network management path rather than a synonym for an arbitrary physical UART header.

Defines ttySx as a serial-port device and documents serial speed/parity/bits/flow-control syntax, supporting separate verification of ttyS0 identity/configuration from physical connector and SOL routing.
Shows that SOL information/activation is an explicit ipmitool LAN+ workflow; actual platform channel, console source and bridge routing remain project/vendor data.

project_authority: The platform/BMC owner resolves physical UART versus SOL/ttyS0 scope, proves console ownership/routing and supplies electrical/serial parameters. An authorized lab operator alone makes and judges the physical connection and harmless interaction. The evidence owner preserves captures, and the end user decides verdict. The future duplicate-code variant remains independently reviewed.
